title: When to Call Your Bank—and When to Just Breathe

 When to Call Your Bank—and When to Just Breathe
Hi Sara,
Let’s talk about something fun.

Debt. Stress. SBA audits.
Okay, so maybe not fun—but definitely important.
If you’ve bought a business (especially an accounting firm), odds are you used SBA financing. And in those first 12–18 months, the transition is often messy.
Cash flow is tight. Clients are adjusting. You’re adjusting. And that loan payment starts to feel… heavy.
So here’s the million-dollar question I hear all the time:
When should I call the bank if I think I might miss a payment?
Here’s the truth:
👉 If you’re just anxious, but still able to pay, breathe. No need to call the bank just to talk about your feelings.
👉 But if it’s looking likely that you’ll miss a payment? Talk to them before it happens.
Silence kills options.

Banks can work with you if the circumstances are right, modify terms, offer temporary forbearance, or extend maturity dates, but only if there’s communication before the problem becomes a disaster.
And if you’re in the first 18 months of your loan, listen up:

That’s the danger zone.
A missed payment triggers an audit by the SBA that puts the bank’s loan guarantee at risk. So yes, they’re extra sensitive during this time. And yes, communication matters more than ever.
Buying a firm is hard enough. Don’t make it harder by ghosting your lender.
To smarter deals (and fewer scary phone calls),
Sara Sharp
Deal Attorney | Founder, Deal Academy
